title: Strawberry pate de fruit
subtitle: firm strawberry fruit jellies set with pectin and rolled in sugar
excerpt: Strawberry pate de fruit are small, firm fruit jellies made from fresh strawberry puree, sugar, and pectin, cooked to a precise temperature and set in a shallow tin. Once cold, they are cut into squares and rolled in caster sugar, which gives them a sparkling, crystalline coating. They keep well and have an intensely concentrated strawberry flavour.
sourceNotes: Pate de fruit is a French confectionery tradition dating to at least the nineteenth century. The technique of cooking fruit puree with pectin and sugar to a precise temperature is documented in French confiserie manuals. Commercial production is particularly associated with the Auvergne region.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks. Do not refrigerate; moisture softens the sugar coating.

content.text: Strawberry pate de fruit are firm fruit jellies with an intensely concentrated flavour and a crystalline sugar coating. Fresh strawberry puree is cooked with pectin and sugar to exactly 107 to 108 degrees C, which gives the set jelly its firm, clean-cutting texture. The temperature is the critical detail: below it and the jelly stays soft; above it and it becomes too hard.
Line a shallow 20 cm square tin with baking paper. Blitz the strawberries to a smooth puree in a blender or food processor. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Weigh out 350 g of puree.
Mix 50 g of the caster sugar with the pectin in a small bowl until combined.

Put the puree and lemon juice in a medium heavy-based saucepan. Bring to the boil over medium heat. Add the pectin-sugar mixture in a steady stream, whisking constantly, then stir in the remaining 350 g of sugar.

Clip on the sugar thermometer and cook over medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until the mixture reaches 107 to 108 degrees C. This takes around 20 minutes and the mixture will thicken and bubble.
Pour immediately into the prepared tin and leave to set at room temperature for at least 3 hours, or overnight.

Turn the set jelly out onto a board dusted with caster sugar. Cut into 2 cm squares with an oiled knife. Roll each square in caster sugar to coat all sides. Store in a single layer in an airtight container.

attrs.problem: Jelly too soft to cut cleanly after setting
attrs.avoid: Avoid removing from the heat before reaching 107 degrees C; the gel will not be firm enough.
attrs.fix: Return the mixture to the saucepan and cook again to the correct temperature. The jelly can be remelted and reset if it has not firmed sufficiently.

attrs.problem: Sugar coating becoming wet and sticky after a day
attrs.avoid: Avoid storing in the fridge; the condensation softens the sugar coating.
attrs.fix: Store at room temperature in an airtight container. If the coating softens, roll the pieces in fresh caster sugar just before serving.
